bio: Emperor Chao of Han, called the "Bright Emperor" in Fir-Flower Tablets, came to the throne as a child in 87 B.C., succeeding his father Emperor Wu. The dates above are those the book's Contents gives.
The archive holds one poem from Fir-Flower Tablets (1921), a song of boating, singing and picking lotus on a clear autumn day.

poems.title: Written in Early Autumn at the Pool of Sprinkling Water
poems.author: Emperor Chao of Han
poems.translator: trans. Florence Ayscough and Amy Lowell (1921)
poems.text:
In Autumn, when the landscape is clear, to float over the wide, water ripples,
To pick the water-chestnut and the lotus-flower with a quick, light hand!
The fresh wind is cool, we start singing to the movement of the oars.
The clouds are bright; they part before the light of dawn; the moon has sunk below the Silver River.
Enjoying such pleasure for ten thousand years--
Could one consider it too much?
